intro.title: Error Boundary
intro.body: In this lesson, you'll build a React component called an Error Boundary that catches JavaScript errors anywhere in its child component tree. You'll learn how to implement the componentDidCatch lifecycle method to handle errors gracefully and display a fallback UI instead of crashing the entire application. The main technologies involved are React class components and lifecycle methods. By the end, you'll understand how to create robust React applications that provide better user experiences when unexpected errors occur.
intro.usecase: Error boundaries are essential in production React applications where components can fail unpredictably. In e-commerce dashboards, they prevent a single faulty product card from crashing the entire product grid. In financial applications, they isolate errors in live data feeds while keeping the main trading interface functional. Social media platforms use them to contain failures in comment threads or media players without breaking the entire post. This pattern gives developers control over failure states while maintaining core user experience.
